ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Three identical square sheets of paper each with side length $6{ }$ are stacked on top of each other. The middle sheet is rotated clockwise $30^\circ$ about its center and the top sheet is rotated clockwise $60^\circ$ about its center, resulting in the $24$-sided polygon shown in the figure below. The area of this polygon can be expressed in the form $a-b\sqrt{c}$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers, and $c$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is $a+b+c?$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: I looked at the attached figure; in the figure there are three square sheets of paper with the same center stacked, with the center marked by a black dot; one square appears to be placed horizontally, and the other two are rotated relative to it, and the outer outline is a symmetric polygon made up of many short sides. The outer shape has a structure that repeats every 30° around the center, consistent with the superposition of three squares with the same side length and angles differing by 30°. Reasoning: The side length of each square is 6, so the half-side length is 3. The directions of the three squares are 0°, 30°, and 60°. Since after the whole is rotated by 30°, this set of directions is equivalent to the original set of directions, it is only necessary to calculate the area of one 30° sector, then multiply by 12. In the sector 0 ≤ θ ≤ 30°, the outer boundary is provided by the square rotated 60°, and is symmetric about θ=15°. For 0 ≤ θ ≤ 15°, the radial distance to the boundary of that square is R(θ)=3/sin(60°−θ). The sector area is (1/2)·2·∫[0 to 15°] (3/sin(60°−θ))^2 dθ = 9∫[0 to π/12] csc^2(π/3−θ)dθ = 9[cot(π/3−θ)]_0^(π/12) = 9(1−1/√3)=9−3√3. The total area is 12(9−3√3)=108−36√3. Therefore a=108, b=36, c=3, so a+b+c=147.

The area of this polygon can be expressed in the form $a-b\sqrt{c}$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers, and $c$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is $a+b+c$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Three identical square sheets of paper each with side length $6$ are stacked on top of each other. The middle sheet is rotated clockwise $30^\circ$ about its center and the top sheet is rotated clockwise $60^\circ$ about its center, resulting in the $24$-sided polygon shown in the figure below. The area of this polygon can be expressed in the form $a-b\sqrt{c}$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers, and $c$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is $a+b+c$?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: I looked at the attached figure; in the figure there are three square sheets of paper with the same center stacked, with the center marked by a black dot; one square appears to be placed horizontally, and the other two are rotated relative to it, and the outer outline is a symmetric polygon made up of many short sides. The outer shape has a structure that repeats every 30° around the center, consistent with the superposition of three squares with the same side length and angles differing by 30°. Reasoning: The side length of each square is 6, so the half-side length is 3. The directions of the three squares are 0°, 30°, and 60°. Since after the whole is rotated by 30°, this set of directions is equivalent to the original set of directions, it is only necessary to calculate the area of one 30° sector, then multiply by 12. In the sector 0 ≤ θ ≤ 30°, the outer boundary is provided by the square rotated 60°, and is symmetric about θ=15°. For 0 ≤ θ ≤ 15°, the radial distance to the boundary of that square is R(θ)=3/sin(60°−θ). The sector area is (1/2)·2·∫[0 to 15°] (3/sin(60°−θ))^2 dθ = 9∫[0 to π/12] csc^2(π/3−θ)dθ = 9[cot(π/3−θ)]_0^(π/12) = 9(1−1/√3)=9−3√3. The total area is 12(9−3√3)=108−36√3. Therefore a=108, b=36, c=3, so a+b+c=147.
